schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE PRODUCT (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    PRODUCT_NAME VARCHAR(255),
    UNIT_PRICE INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (UNIT_PRICE > 0)
);

CREATE TABLE SALES (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    SELLER_ID INT,
    BUYER_ID INT,
    SALE_DATE DATE,
    QUANTITY INT,
    PRICE INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (PRODUCT_ID) REFERENCES PRODUCT(PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (QUANTITY > 0),
    CHECK (PRICE > 0)
);
q1: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2: SELECT S.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN SALES S ON S.PRODUCT_ID = P.PRODUCT_ID GROUP BY S.PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(S.SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(S.SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31'

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 filters products whose sales records (as a group) have all sale dates between '2019-01-01' and '2019-03-31'. Q2 filters products based on the same aggregate conditions but may return duplicate rows for the same product if multiple rows exist in SALES for the same product (since Q2 does not use a subquery to deduplicate). Q2 may return multiple rows per product if SALES has multiple rows for the same product.
counterexample_dsp: A product with sales on '2019-01-01' and '2019-04-01'. Q1 will exclude it because MAX(SALE_DATE) > '2019-03-31', while Q2 will also exclude it. A product with sales only on '2019-02-15' will be included by both. A product with multiple sales rows within the date range will be included by both. The difference is not clear in this case.
